sourceLabel: Univ. of South Carolina Math 550 review, Vector Inequalities
evidence: Proof uses u.v=|u||v|cos(theta) and |cos|<=1, which is the second half of the sketch. The parallelogram-area / sin theta step is absent from every source read.
sketchProblem: The area step (area >= 0 = |x||y||sin theta|) contributes nothing to the conclusion; the real content is the angle definition plus |cos theta|<=1 (and the angle definition itself presupposes C-S for it to be well defined, so the route is circular as a foundation).

sourceLabel: Arav, Hall, Li, Cauchy-Schwarz for three vectors (Math. Inequal. Appl. 2008)
evidence: States that nonnegativity of the 2x2 Gramian is equivalent to Cauchy-Schwarz, citing a reference; no proof that the Gram matrix is positive semidefinite or that its determinant is >=0 is given for the 2-vector case.

sourceLabel: Univ. of South Carolina Math 550 review, Vector Inequalities
evidence: Proof expands ||u+v||^2 and applies Cauchy-Schwarz (algebraic), not a shortest-path/geometry argument. Wikipedia Triangle inequality only gives the polygonal-path/arc-length corollary, not the Euclidean-norm proof from straight-segment minimality.
sketchProblem: The sketch takes "Euclidean distance is the shortest path" as given, which is itself the triangle inequality, so as written it is circular unless a separate geometric proof of the segment minimality is supplied.

sourceLabel: Semmes, Another introduction to the geometry of metric spaces (arXiv 0710.2690)
evidence: Proves that convexity of the unit ball B_N implies the triangle inequality by exactly the convex combination t=N(x)/(N(x)+N(y)) of x/N(x), y/N(y). Convexity of the Euclidean ball is only asserted ("one can use convexity of r^2"), which matches the sketch's own assumption.
sketchProblem: Not independent: convexity of the Euclidean ball is itself shown via convexity of r^2 or Cauchy-Schwarz, as the sketch admits.

preciseLocator: Section "Proofs" > "Trigonometric proof using the law of cosines"
